377968.title: Torsion characterization by stable torsion length
377968.statement:
Let $\operatorname{Mod}_g$ be the mapping class group of a closed orientable surface of genus $g$. For $f\in\operatorname{Mod}_g$, let $\tau_g(f)$ be the minimum number of torsion elements whose product is $f$, and define the stable torsion length by

$$
||f||_{\tau_g}=\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{\tau_g(f^n)}{n}.
$$

**Stable torsion length conjecture.** If

$$
||f||_{\tau_g}=0,
$$

then $f$ is torsion.
This is presented as a stronger version of the conjecture on Dehn twists. The source notes that torsion elements have stable torsion length zero, but gives no resolution of the converse.
377968.review_depth: full source note read (Korkmaz math/0307146, Conjecture 2); prior-art body read (Kotschick math/0307362, Example ex:involutions and the mapping-class example)
377968.summary: Conjecture 2 (||f||_tau=0 implies f torsion) is false: if f=st with s,t involutions then f^n is a product of at most two torsion elements, so ||f||_tau=0, and products of two involutions of infinite order exist in Mod_g (e.g. iota * t_b iota t_b^{-1} = t_{iota(b)} t_b^{-1}). Independently derived here, but already in Kotschick (2003/2004), who also cites McCarthy-Papadopoulos pseudo-Anosov products of involutions.

377973.title: Kostov's irreducible Deligne–Simpson criterion
377973.statement:
Let $C_1,\ldots,C_k$ be the prescribed conjugacy classes, and let $A_i\in C_i$. Let $\alpha$ be the associated dimension vector, let $\xi^{[\delta]}$ denote the scalar attached to a positive root $\delta$, and let $p(\delta)$ be the corresponding function on dimension vectors. An **irreducible solution** means a solution whose matrices $A_i$ have no common invariant subspace.

**Kostov's conjecture.** There is an irreducible solution to

$$
A_1\dots A_k=1
$$

with $A_i\in C_i$ if and only if $\alpha$ is a positive root, $\xi^{[\alpha]}=1$, and

$$
p(\alpha)>p(\beta)+p(\gamma)+\dots
$$

for every nontrivial decomposition $\alpha=\beta+\gamma+\dots$ into positive roots satisfying $\xi^{[\beta]}=\xi^{[\gamma]}=\dots=1$.

This is the irreducible form of the Deligne–Simpson problem, which asks for matrices in prescribed conjugacy classes whose product is the identity. The criterion is presented here as a conjecture; the supplied source gives no resolution evidence.

378033.title: Conjecture on local maxima for Sendov's conjecture
378033.statement:
Let $S_n$ be the set of monic complex polynomials of degree $n\ge 2$ whose zeros lie in the closed unit disk, and let

$$
d(p)=\max_{z\in Z(p)}\min_{w\in Z(p')}|z-w|.
$$

A polynomial is **locally maximal for Sendov's conjecture** if it is a local maximum of $d$ on $S_n$. **The local-maxima conjecture.** The polynomials $z^n+e^{i\theta}$, with $\theta\in\mathbf{R}$, are all the local maxima for $d$; equivalently, a polynomial $p\in S_n$ is locally maximal for Sendov's conjecture if and only if $p(z)=z^n+e^{i\theta}$ for some $\theta\in\mathbf{R}$. The source presents this as a stronger version of the extremal-polynomial conjecture and gives no resolution.

378034.title: Spectral variation conjecture for normal operators and differentiator compressions
378034.statement:
Let $A$ be a normal operator on a complex Hilbert space of dimension $n\ge 2$. Let $\rho(A)$ denote the radius of the smallest closed disk containing the spectrum of $A$, let $A'$ be the compression of $A$ to the orthogonal complement of a trace vector of $A$, and let $s(A,A')$ denote the spectral variation between $A$ and $A'$. **The spectral variation conjecture.** One has

$$
s(A,A')\le \rho(A),
$$

and equality occurs if and only if either $A=0$, or $A$ has simple eigenvalues and $A^n$ is a non-zero scalar operator. The claim reformulates the polynomial conjectures in terms of spectra of a normal operator and its compression. The source gives no resolution, so the conjecture remains open there.

378069.title: Boden–Hu conjecture on small resolutions of parabolic bundle moduli spaces
378069.statement:
Let $N$ and $s$ be integers with $0<s<N$, and let

$$
W(N,s)^{\circ}:=\{\alpha\in\mathbb{R}^N:0<\alpha_1<\cdots<\alpha_N<1\text{ and }\sum_{n=1}^N\alpha_n=s\}.
$$

For $\alpha\in W(N,s)^{\circ}$, let $M(\underline{\mathbf{1}})^\alpha$ be the moduli scheme of quasiparabolic bundles with multiplicity vector $\underline{\mathbf{1}}=(N,-s,1,\ldots,1)$, and for a generic weight vector $\beta$ near $\alpha$ let

$$
\phi_\beta:M(\underline{\mathbf{1}})^\beta\longrightarrow M(\underline{\mathbf{1}})^\alpha
$$

be the canonical morphism induced by the identity functor. A morphism is **small** if the locus where its fibers have dimension at least $k$ has codimension greater than $2k$ for every positive integer $k$. **Boden–Hu conjecture.** Near every $\alpha\in W(N,s)^{\circ}$, there is a generic $\beta\in W(N,s)^{\circ}$ such that $\phi_\beta$ is a small map. This predicts that every moduli space arising from an arbitrary weight vector admits, locally in weight space, a generic-weight resolution with no divisorial exceptional contribution. The supplied text does not state whether the conjecture is open or resolved.

378069.summary: Source title and introduction: the Boden-Hu conjecture holds precisely up to rank eight (N <= 8); Proposition examples gives counterexamples in all other cases (Section Counterexamples).

378115.title: The motivic fundamental lemma
378115.statement:
Let $\mathbb{K}$ be the motivic coefficient ring described in the source, let $(\mathfrak{g},\mathfrak{h})$ be a pair in Definition~, and let $r\in\mathbb{Q}$. For the varieties $U(\mathfrak{g},\mathfrak{h},r)_i$, coefficients $b(\mathfrak{g},\mathfrak{h},r)_i$, index sets $I(\mathfrak{g},\mathfrak{h},r)$, and polynomials $p(\mathfrak{g},\mathfrak{h},r)$ introduced earlier, the relevant classes lie in $\mathbb{K}$.

**Motivic fundamental lemma.** For every such pair and every $r\in\mathbb{Q}$, one has the identity in $\mathbb{K}$

$$
p(\mathfrak{h},\mathfrak{h},r)(\mathbb{L})\sum_{i\in I(\mathfrak{g},\mathfrak{h},r)} b(\mathfrak{g},\mathfrak{h},r)_i[U(\mathfrak{g},\mathfrak{h},r)_i]
 =p(\mathfrak{g},\mathfrak{h},r)(\mathbb{L})\sum_{i\in I(\mathfrak{h},\mathfrak{h},r)} b(\mathfrak{h},\mathfrak{h},r)_i[U(\mathfrak{h},\mathfrak{h},r)_i].
$$

This is the geometric or motivic form of the fundamental lemma: after cross-multiplying the denominators from the preceding variety formula, it predicts an identity of motivic classes. The source does not state a resolution status for this conjecture.

378162.title: The majorization conjecture for twisted root maps
378162.statement:
Let $\mathcal{C}_n$ be the class of polynomials of degree $n$ under consideration, let $\mathcal{A}'$ be the class of operators defined in the paper, and write $Z(P)$ for the multiset of zeros of a polynomial $P$. For a vector, $\Re$ and $\Im$ denote its componentwise real and imaginary parts, and $\prec$ denotes classical majorization.

**Majorization conjecture.** If $T\in\mathcal{A}'$ and $n\ge 1$, then for every $P\in\mathcal{C}_n$ at least one of the relations

$$
\Re Z(P)\prec \Re Z\bigl(T(P)\bigr),\qquad \Im Z\bigl(T(P)\bigr)\prec \Im Z(P)
$$

is valid.

The conjecture proposes a global alternative between majorization of the real parts in the forward direction and majorization of the imaginary parts in the reverse direction for the operators under study. It is motivated by numerical experiments and by local results for real parameters, while the preceding counterexamples show that analogous complex statements involving convex-hull inclusion or stronger forms of majorization cannot hold generally.

378285.title: Andrews's modified partition identity for $A_{4,3,3}(n)$
378285.statement:
Let $A_{4,3,3}(n)$ be the partition-counting function defined by the conditions for even $lambda=4$, and let $B_{4,3,3}(n)$ count partitions satisfying the stated difference and multiplicity conditions, where $f_j$ denotes the number of appearances of $j$. Define $B^0_{4,3,3}(n)$ by imposing in addition

$$
f_{5j+2}+f_{5j+3}\leq 1\quad (j\geq 0),
$$

$$
f_{5j+4}+f_{5j+6}\leq 1\quad (j\geq 0),
$$

$$
f_{5j-1}+f_{5j}+f_{5j+5}+f_{5j+6}\leq 3\quad (j\geq 1).
$$

**Andrews's conjecture.** For every positive integer $n$,

$$
A_{4,3,3}(n)=B^0_{4,3,3}(n).
$$

The conjecture gives a modification of the partition conditions in Andrews's theorem that admits the case $k<\lambda$; the source presents it as a conjecture attributed to Andrews. The paper's title indicates that this particular identity is subsequently proved by an analytic argument.

378324.title: Pemantle–Steif phase-transition conjecture for Heisenberg models
378324.statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be a tree with branching number $\operatorname{br}(\Gamma)$, let $d\geq 1$, and let $\rho^d(J)$ denote the first normalized spherical harmonic coefficient associated with the $d$-dimensional Heisenberg interaction at parameter $J$.

$$
\operatorname{br}(\Gamma)\rho^d(J)<1,
$$

then the $d$-dimensional Heisenberg model on $\Gamma$ with parameter $J$ does not exhibit a phase transition.

The paper proves the corresponding criterion for robust phase transition and notes that the conjecture would establish coincidence of phase transition and robust phase transition for Heisenberg models. It also proves the claim when the branching number is $1$.

378371.title: The refined Rubin–Stark reciprocity conjecture
378371.statement:
Let $p$ be an odd prime splitting completely in $k$, let $K/k$ and the other notation be as in the paper, and let $G=\operatorname{Gal}(K/k)$. in $({\mathbb Z}/p^{n+1}{\mathbb Z})G$ for all $\theta\in\bigwedge^d_{{\mathbb Z}_pG}U_p^1(K)$. This is the refined reciprocity statement sought after the rational Rubin–Stark element is introduced. The paper formulates it as a conjectural identity; no resolution is supplied.

$$
p \leq q \leq r.
$$

Then all facets of $P_\Delta^{p,q,r}$ are obtained by collapsing from facets of $P_\Delta^{p,q,q}$.

378465.title: Clarke–Hochberg–Hurlbert connectivity conjecture for graph pebbling
378465.statement: Let $d\ge 1$. 378528.title: Majid's conjecture on the quadratic differential algebra of simply-laced Weyl groups
378528.statement:
Let $W$ be a Weyl group, let ${\cal C}$ be its set of reflections, and let $\Lambda_w$ be the left-invariant differential algebra associated with this differential structure. Let $\Lambda^1$ be its space of left-invariant one-forms, and define the quadratic algebra

$$
\Lambda_{quad}:=T_K\Lambda^1/\operatorname{ker}(1-\Psi),
$$

where $\Psi$ is the braiding. For a simply-laced root system, **Majid's conjecture.**

$$
\Lambda_w\cong\Lambda_{quad}.
$$

For type $A$ root systems, this conjecture was stated by S. Majid. It asserts that the quadratic relations determine the full left-invariant differential algebra in the simply-laced case; its status is not specified in the source.

378574.title: The rectangle lower-bound conjecture for the Cauchy-process spectral gap
378574.statement:
Let $D\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ be a bounded convex domain symmetric with respect to both coordinate axes. Let $R$ be the smallest rectangle containing $D$ whose sides are parallel to the coordinate axes. For $0<\alpha<2$, let $\lambda_1$ and $\lambda_2$ denote the first two eigenvalues of the symmetric $\alpha$-stable process killed upon exiting the indicated domain. **Rectangle lower-bound conjecture.**

$$
\lambda_2(R)-\lambda_1(R)\leq\lambda_2(D)-\lambda_1(D).
$$

This is proposed as a sharp lower bound for the spectral gap in the symmetric stable-process setting. The source gives no resolution for $0<\alpha<2$; it contrasts this lower-bound question with the Brownian-motion case and discusses related stable-process inequalities.

378584.title: Lexicographically least extremal permutation conjecture
378584.statement:
Let $n>2$ be prime, and define a permutation $g$ of $\mathbb Z_n$ by

$$
g(x)=\begin{cases}x/(x-1)&\text{if }x\neq1,\\1&\text{if }x=1.

378637.title: Green's cap-set exponent conjecture over \(\mathbb F_3^n\)
378637.statement:
Let $r_3(\mathbb{F}_3^n)$ be the largest size of a subset of $\mathbb{F}_3^n$ containing no three-term arithmetic progression, and let

$$
\mu(3):=\limsup_{n\to\infty}\frac{\log_3(r_3(\mathbb{F}_3^n))}{n}.
$$

**Green's conjecture.** $\mu(3)<1$. Equivalently, there is an absolute constant $\delta>0$ such that

$$
r_3(\mathbb{F}_3^n)\leqslant (3-\delta)^n.
$$

This asserts an exponentially smaller upper bound than the trivial estimate for cap sets in $\mathbb F_3^n$. The source presents it as a belief opposing the possibility $\mu(3)=1$; no resolution is supplied here.

378663.title: Bacher's conjecture on Bernoulli-number numerator quotients
378663.statement:
Let $B_n$ be the Bernoulli numbers, let $(p,l)$ be an irregular pair with smallest $l$ when the index of irregularity $i(p)>1$, and let $\operatorname{num}(r)$ denote the numerator of a rational number $r$. Define

$$
A(p)=\min_m\left\{m\,\middle|\,\operatorname{num}\left(\frac{B_m}{m}\right)\Big/\operatorname{num}\left(\frac{B_m}{m(m-1)}\right)=p\right\}.
$$

**Bacher's conjecture.** Then $A(p)=(l-1)p+1$.

This conjecture concerns the numerators of the Bernoulli-number quotients $B_m/m$ and $B_m/(m(m-1))$ and was suggested by Roland Bacher in connection with Integer Sequence A092291. The paper later gives an equivalent formulation in terms of irregular pairs and proves a criterion for when the claimed value is valid; the conjectural assertion is not resolved here.

378665.title: Matsuki–Gindikin conjecture on domains associated with flag-manifold orbits
378665.statement:
Let $G_\mathbb C$ be a connected complex semisimple Lie group, let $G_\mathbb R$ be a connected real form, and let $K_\mathbb C$ be the complexification of a maximal compact subgroup of $G_\mathbb R$. Let $X=G_\mathbb C/P$ be a flag manifold that is not $K_\mathbb C$-homogeneous. For each $K_\mathbb C$-orbit $S$ on $X$, let $C(S)$ be the associated $G_\mathbb R$-$K_\mathbb C$-invariant subset of $G_\mathbb C$, and let $C(S)_0$ denote its connected component containing the identity. Let $D$ be the Akhiezer–Gindikin domain.

**Matsuki–Gindikin conjecture.** For every $K_\mathbb C$-orbit $S$ of nonholomorphic type on $X$, one has

$$
C(S)_0=D.
$$

The conjecture concerns the equivalence of domains arising from duality between $K_\mathbb C$- and $G_\mathbb R$-orbits on flag manifolds. The source states that it was already proved for closed and open orbits, for the remaining orbits when $G_\mathbb R$ is of non-Hermitian type, and, in this paper, for arbitrary non-closed orbits when $G_\mathbb R$ is of Hermitian type; thus it is completely solved affirmatively.

378697.title: Huneke–Srinivasan multiplicity conjecture
378697.statement:
Let $R=k[x_0,\dots,x_n]$, and let $J\subset R$ be a homogeneous ideal of codimension $c$ such that $R/J$ is Cohen–Macaulay. Let $e(R/J)$ denote the multiplicity of $R/J$. For the minimal graded free resolution of $R/J$, let $m_i$ be the minimal degree of a syzygy at step $i$, and let $M_i$ be the corresponding maximum.

**Huneke–Srinivasan multiplicity conjecture.** One has

$$
\frac{1}{c!}\prod_{i=1}^c m_i\le e(R/J)\le\frac{1}{c!}\prod_{i=1}^c M_i.
$$

This conjecture concerns sharp multiplicity bounds in terms of the degree shifts in a Cohen–Macaulay graded resolution. The supplied context says it is known in a number of special cases but remains open in general, even for monomial ideals in codimension three and above.

378771.title: The Shimura correspondence central-value formula for level $p^2$
378771.statement:
Let $p$ be the prime and let $f$ be the weight-$2$ eigenform introduced in the construction above. Fix $\sigma\in\{+,-\}$, and let $c_f(d)$ be the coefficient of $q^d$ in

$$
\Theta_f^\sigma=\sum_{\left(\frac{d}{p}\right)=\sigma}c_f(d)q^d.
$$

Let $\alpha_f$ be the rational constant defined according as $f$ is not a twist of a level-$p$ form, is the quadratic twist of a level-$p$ form, or is a level-$p$ form. **The Shimura correspondence central-value formula.** For every integer $d$ such that $-pd<0$ is a fundamental discriminant and $\left(\frac{d}{p}\right)=\sigma$,

$$
L(f,-pd,1)L(f,1)=\alpha_f\,\frac{\langle f,f\rangle}{\sqrt{pd}}\frac{c_f(d)^2}{\langle\e{f}^{\sigma},\e{f}^{\sigma}\rangle}.
$$

This formula relates central values of twisted $L$-functions to Fourier coefficients arising from the quaternionic Shimura correspondence, with the normalization depending on the choice of $\e{f}^{\sigma}$. The supplied text states the identity but gives no evidence resolving whether it is intended as a conjecture or as a theorem.

378902.title: The lower-bound conjecture for the zero-sum-free sequence constant
378902.statement:
Let $n>1$ be a positive integer, and let $p$ be the smallest prime divisor of $n$. For positive integers $n$ and $k$, let

$$
h(n,k)=\min\{h(S)\mid |S|=n+k\},
$$

where $S$ ranges over sequences in $\mathbb{Z}_n$ of length $n+k$ such that $0\notin\sum_n(S)$. **Lower-bound conjecture.** If $k\geq (n/p)-1$, then

$$
h(n,k)\geq k+1.
$$

This conjecture extends known lower bounds for $h(n,k)$ and addresses the range in which the previously expected bound has counterexamples. Its status is unresolved in the supplied source.

378981.title: Oppenheim's conjecture on lattices with positive norm minimum
378981.statement:
Let $n\geqslant 3$ and let $\Lambda\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be an $n$-dimensional lattice with positive norm minimum $N(\Lambda)>0$. A lattice is called **algebraic** when it is similar, modulo the action of the group of diagonal $n\times n$ matrices, to the lattice of a complete module of a totally real algebraic field of degree $n$. **Oppenheim's conjecture.** The lattice $\Lambda$ is algebraic.

The converse is an obvious consequence of the Dirichlet theorem on algebraic units, while the conjecture itself remains unproved. In dimension three it implies Littlewood's conjecture, and attempted proofs in dimensions three and higher contained an essential gap.

379012.title: The multiplicity conjecture for finitely generated graded torsion modules
379012.statement:
Let $R=k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ be a standard graded polynomial ring over a field, and let $N$ be a finitely generated graded torsion $R$-module. Set $c=n-\dim N$ and, for a minimal graded free resolution of $N$, let $m_0$ be the minimum shift in homological degree zero and $M_i$ the maximum shift in homological degree $i$. **Multiplicity conjecture for torsion modules.** One has

$$
e(N)\leq\frac{1}{c!}\prod_{i=1}^c(M_i-m_0),
$$

with equality if and only if $N$ is Cohen–Macaulay and has a pure resolution. This extends the multiplicity conjecture from cyclic modules to finitely generated graded torsion modules; the paper proposes the bound and establishes it for torsion modules of codimension at most two, while the general statement remains open.

379043.title: Maximum colourful simplicial depth conjecture
379043.statement:
Let a colourful configuration consist of $(d+1)$ points in each of $(d+1)$ colours in $d$-dimensional space. Its **core** is the intersection of the convex hulls of the individual colours. For a point $p$ in the interior of the core, the colourful simplicial depth is the number of colourful simplices containing $p$, where a colourful simplex has one vertex of each colour. Let $
u(d)$ denote the maximum of this depth over such configurations and points.

**Maximum colourful simplicial depth conjecture.** The maximum colourful simplicial depth of any point in the interior of the core is

$$
\nu(d)=d^{d+1}+1.
$$

A construction gives the lower bound $\nu(d)\geq d^{d+1}+1$, and the conjecture asserts that this bound is tight; the authors report that a computer search found no counterexamples.

379064.title: The maximum critical-value conjecture for families of L-functions
379064.statement:
Let $\mathcal F$ be a family of $L$-functions, and for $F\in\mathcal F$ let $c(F)$ denote its conductor. Assume the family is ordered by conductor and has approximately $D$ members with conductor below $D$. For unitary families set $B=1/2$, and for symplectic or orthogonal families set $B=1$. **Maximum critical-value conjecture.**

$$
\max_{\substack{F\in\mathcal F\\c(F)\le D}}|F(\tfrac12)|=\exp\left((1+o(1))\sqrt{B\log D\log\log D}\right).
$$

The implied constant depends only on $\mathcal F$. This extends the zeta maximum-size prediction to families of $L$-functions, with the symmetry type determining the constant in the exponent.
